issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies the lecture attributes as private (indicated by '-' in the class diagram), and the solution implementation declares them private. However, the template Lecture.java already declares two attributes (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents) as public. This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation (whether fields should be private with getters/setters) and may lead them to follow the inconsistent visibility when adding the remaining attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Lecture.java fields consistent with the UML and the solution by declaring the attributes private (e.g., private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents;) and keep the TODOs for students to add the remaining private attributes and corresponding getters/setters. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to indicate public fields if exposing them is intentional.
